prompt_text: John have 10 apples. He gives 5 to Mary who eat 2 for lunch. John buys two more apples. How many apples do they have?
response_text:
John starts with 10 apples.  
- He gives 5 to Mary → John has \(10-5 = 5\) apples.  
- Mary eats 2 → Mary has \(5-2 = 3\) apples left.  
- John buys 2 more → John has \(5+2 = 7\) apples.

So together they have  
\(7\) (John) \(+\) \(3\) (Mary) \(=\boxed{10}\) apples.
